newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - March 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - March 4.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Tuesday's Daily Variety:

* HOLLYWOOD - Former Los Angeles Lakers superstar Earvin (Magic) Johnson has agreed to develop, produce and host a new syndicated latenight talk-variety strip for News Corp Twentieth TV, which may be on the air by next year.

* HOLLYWOOD - Bruce Willis' "Broadway Brawler" movie shut down Friday after 20 days filming. Director Lee Grant and producer/husband Joe Feury have been fired, while rumors are flying about which cast members will remain and how much of the film will be retained.

* LAS VEGAS - Frank Mancuso, the chairman of Kirk Kerkorian's Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer, blamed Hollywood studios and nationwide exhibitors for driving the industry to a dangerous precipice with their determination to build more theaters and release more movies. "We've lost our sense of restraint, continually overproducing and overbuilding," Mancuso told exhibitors in his keynote address during NATO ShoWest at Bally's Hotel. Mancuso offered a five-point plan, including cutting back on production and a joint industry campaign with studios and exhibitors to bring the public back into the theaters.

* HOLLYWOOD - Casey Silver, who has been with Seagram-owned Universal for nine years and has served as chairman of the motion picture group since 1994, has been given oversight of Universal's homevideo wing.
* HOLLYWOOD - Gotham stage director Julie Taymor has signed on with First Look Pictures for a feature film version of Shakespeare's "Titus Andronicus."

* NEW YORK - After pulling out of one ABC series built around him, Jim Belushi has committed to co-star in "Total Security," the Steven Bochco-created drama for ABC. Belushi will star with James Remar in the series, which will begin airing this fall with a 13-episode commitment. In "Total Security," Remar plays the owner of a high-tech security firm. Belushi is his former classmate at the police academy who wants to join his firm, though Remar wants nothing to do with him. ABC is owned by Walt Disney.
